workLog.phase: Measure the gate failure and trace every orphan
actions: Ran scan.py on default targets against clean main and got VERDICT: CRITICAL_FAIL with 32 findings across 12 spec files
Grouped findings by referenced entity: 24 point at one retired script and the remaining 8 split across five more
Ran git log --diff-filter=D on each missing path to find the commit that removed it, rather than guessing whether a replacement exists
workLog.outcome: 32 findings on 30 distinct lines across 12 files, every one traced to a deliberate deletion: #2187 retired the count validator, #3432 removed the bundle registry as dead code, #1141 migrated the traceability script to Python, #610 renamed the session-end validator, and of the two skill names, session-qa-eligibility was folded into `session` while session-migration was sunset in #2359 (commit 59e6587c46)

workLog.phase: Check whether the repo had already decided this question
actions: Found .agents/critique/001-fix-validate-sessionend-references-critique.md, which rejected an earlier plan for rewriting historical records
Confirmed the current correction already lives in .claude/commands/build.md, which states the old marketplace count validator has been retired and points contributors at the ignore directives
Read .agents/specs/STATUS.md, which documents the repo's supersession convention: mark the status, cite the successor, keep the file in place
workLog.outcome: Rewriting the original prose would introduce anachronism the repo has already ruled against, but the repo does have a convention for marking a spec superseded, which is annotation rather than rewriting

workLog.phase: Choose the narrower of the two escape hatches
actions: Read the directive table in the skill: file scope skips the whole file, line scope skips one line

Counted base-tree precedent at d544eaa60a with git grep -oh -F on markdown files only: 25 line-scope and 22 file-scope directives already present. Dropping the markdown filter gives 31 and 23, but the extra 6 are the validator's own patterns.py, its mirror, a test, and a session log, which are the directive's implementation rather than documents using it
Chose line scope because the skill's own anti-pattern list warns that file scope on a spec masks real orphans, and these specs stay in the scan
workLog.outcome: 30 directives across 12 files, verified by diff to be pure suffix appends with no prose changed. Landed as three commits. The branch has since been rebased onto origin/main, so those original SHAs are no longer reachable from it. The objects still exist, so git show resolves them

workLog.phase: Adversarial review caught that the directives alone were dishonest
actions: Ran a review on a different model with the explicit question: is any silenced line an active instruction rather than historical narrative

The reviewer flagged that the specs carry status draft, todo, and in-progress, and that many flagged lines are imperative: Create bundle_registry.py, MUST import from, shall replace the hard-coded PLUGIN_COUNTERS dict, THE SYSTEM SHALL invoke

Verified the reviewer rather than trusting it: tests/test_command_bundles.py no longer exists, and git grep over *.py returns no definition or consumer of BUNDLE_REGISTRY or PLUGIN_COUNTERS, so those instructions are unimplementable as written. Both names still appear in spec and ADR prose, which is narrative rather than live code
Also verified two false claims in the first draft of this log: the precedent counts were 25 and 22, not 39 and 29, and the 32 findings sit on 30 lines, not 32
Annotated the design and task tiers: TASK-009 line 70 tells an implementer to mirror COUNT_PATTERN and LABEL_MAP byte-for-byte from the deleted script, and neither name exists in patterns.py today

Annotated SPEC-005 last: TASK-005 is status todo and says Create scripts/validation/bundle_registry.py and MUST import from it, but git shows that file created in 7310d0c9c4 then deleted in #3432 with tests/test_command_bundles.py, and git grep over *.py returns no definition or consumer of BUNDLE_REGISTRY today
workLog.outcome: Added a dated retirement note after the H1 of ten of the thirteen affected specs naming the removed dependency, the PR, and the commit, and stating the instructions below are no longer actionable. The directives now sit under a banner that tells the reader the truth instead of hiding a live contract pointing at a deleted file

workLog.phase: Second adversarial pass caught three defects in the fix itself
actions: Sent the annotated branch back to the same reviewer with the explicit question: is the banner sufficient, and is every SHA in it correct
Reviewer returned three blockers. Verified each with git rather than accepting them, and all three held

Blocker one: seven notes closed with the sentence Count claims are now scanned by the orphan-ref-validator skill, which is false. The scanner emits only skill_name, script_path, and scan_truncated. counts.py does catalog enumeration, not count-claim scanning. The file is the original count subsystem from #1979, gutted in #2853; #3434 added sibling-namespace enumeration to the same file. The name is a fossil

Blocker two: git log -S COUNT_CLAIM_RE shows COUNT_PATTERN, COUNT_CLAIM_RE, COUNT_LABEL_MAP, and extract_count_claims did land, then were retired in #2853 (commit 9c88990b77) to mirror the validator deleted in #2187. The earlier claim that they never landed was wrong; the instruction is retired, not unreachable

Blocker three: REQ-005 is status draft, its AC-14 requires pre_pr.py to run bundle coverage, and pre_pr.py has no bundle check. DESIGN-005 and TASK-005 carry banners while their parent requirement did not, so the fix left two of three tiers marked dead and the third reading as live
Also confirmed the notes carried no date despite this log calling them dated, and that session-migration was sunset in #2359 rather than folded into session
workLog.outcome: Replaced the false count-scan sentence in seven notes with the #2853 retirement, dated all ten notes, added the missing REQ-005 banner, and corrected six further claims in this log. Two of the three blockers were defects this fix introduced, not pre-existing ones, which is the argument for reviewing the remediation and not just the original change

nextSteps: Re-scope REQ-003 and REQ-015 if either is resumed: both specify work against a script that no longer exists (issue #3449)
Extend UPSTREAM_PATTERNS in scripts/validation/check_skill_md_portability.py with templates/agents/ and templates/platforms/ only

The episode extractor short-circuits on endingCommit: _collect_shas calls _SHA_RE.findall on that field first and returns immediately once it has anything, so the workLog fallback never runs and the episode records exactly one commit however many the session made. Verified by calling _collect_shas on this log, which returns a single SHA while the branch carries many. No count is stated here because any figure would change with the commit that records it
endingCommit records the last content commit on this branch. The commit that writes the field necessarily follows it, and the PR squash-merges, so neither SHA reaches main
